source_of_truth: Read by hand across two files: addComment() reads getSession() (so authorization is visible and present) and runs its input through assertValid(), whose body in check.ts rejects a non-string, empty, or over-long body. So the action both authorizes and validates. The action's own body does not contain any token from the auditor's validation vocabulary (no z./safeParse/schema/validate), so the single-file heuristic has insufficient evidence to assert that validation is missing; a correct auditor must not claim server-action-without-validation here.

forbidden.why_not_a_defect: the action awaits getSession() before using the identity; authorization is visible and present.
input is validated by assertValid(), which enforces type and length; the file just does not use a recognizable validation-library token.
